name: planet_parameters
label: Planet parameters
description: Each planet's orbital and physical parameters with their uncertainties.
system_prompt: Extract exoplanet parameters from an astronomy paper, exactly as the paper reports them.
intro: For every planet (or substellar companion) in the structure plan below, extract the planet's orbital and physical parameters the paper reports. The structure plan's sets are host stars (planetary systems) and its samples are planets: give each value the planet's set_label and sample_label.

parameters.description: argument of periastron omega (give the unit as printed, e.g. rad)
epoch (time) of periastron T_p (give the unit as printed, e.g. 'JD-2450000' or 'BJD-2450000')
minimum mass M_p sin i (give the unit as printed: M_J, M_E, ...)
true planet mass (not M sin i), e.g. from astrometry or transits + RV
transit midpoint (give the unit as printed, e.g. 'BJD-2450000')
ratio of semi-major axis to stellar radius a/R*
ratio of planet to stellar radius Rp/R*
time reference frame of the epochs, e.g. 'BJD_TDB', 'JD'

rules: Report the values THIS paper gives for each planet -- its own fit, or the values it adopts and uses (then say in `note` where they come from, e.g. 'adopted from Takeda et al. 2008'). Don't fill in values from other papers that this paper only mentions in passing.
When a value is given in several places (abstract, text, table), use the table value with its uncertainties.
Asymmetric uncertainties are printed as superscript/subscript (e.g. 323.21 +0.06 -0.05): `err_plus` 0.06, `err_minus` -0.05.
A value marked '(fixed)' was fixed in the fit, not measured: give it with no uncertainties and say so in `note`.
Minimum mass (M sin i) and true mass are different parameters: an RV-only fit gives M sin i (pl_msinij); give pl_massj only when the paper derives the true mass (inclination known).

A planet with several samples (one per solution, the solution in [brackets] in its sample_label) gets each solution's values on its own sample_label -- never mix values from different solutions on one row.
